description.value: Students follow a full development lifecycle to create an interactive text-based adventure game that leverages generative AI APIs for dynamic storytelling. They decompose complex problems into user stories and design prototypes that prioritise user experience before implementing their solution using modular, object-oriented programming techniques. The project concludes with a multimodal evaluation where students validate their data handling processes and critique the ethical implications and enterprise opportunities of their AI-driven system.

conditions.value:
• 4–6 weeks of class time with opportunities for supervised and independent development.
• Project Portfolio (Digital): 8–10 A4 pages or equivalent digital media.
• Submission components: Decomposed user stories, design criteria, algorithmic designs (flowcharts and pseudocode), modular source code (object-oriented), and data validation/test cases.
• Multimodal Evaluation: 2–3 minute recorded demonstration and critique, or 800–1000 words of written analytical text.
• Resources: Access to an integrated development environment (IDE), generative AI APIs, and digital design tools.
• Authentication: Teacher observation of progressive development and verification of original code through school-approved plagiarism and AI-usage protocols.

resourcesAvailable.value:
Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) such as github codespaces for modular, object-oriented programming. 

Access to generative AI API endpoints (e.g., OpenAI, Google Gemini) and technical documentation for JSON data handling and request authentication.

Design and prototyping software such as Figma, Lucidchart, or Draw.io for user experience mapping and flowchart development.

Unit-specific templates for stakeholder interviewing, user story development, and structured test cases.

context.value: In this unit, students explore the integration of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to design and develop a sophisticated text-based adventure game. They apply design thinking to generate and prototype user experiences that leverage dynamic AI-generated content. They represent their solution logic through detailed flowcharts and pseudocode, which are then implemented using an object-oriented programming language. Throughout the development phase, students validate their algorithms and use specific test cases to ensure narrative consistency and technical robustness. Finally, students critique the digital footprint and ethical implications of generative AI, evaluating their projects against design criteria that consider enterprise opportunities and the future impact of automated content generation in a global context.

task.value: Students follow a full development lifecycle to create an interactive text-based adventure game that leverages generative AI APIs for dynamic storytelling. They decompose complex problems into user stories and design prototypes that prioritise user experience before implementing their solution using modular, object-oriented programming techniques. The project concludes with a multimodal evaluation where students validate their data handling processes and critique the ethical implications and enterprise opportunities of their AI-driven system.

toComplete.value:
To complete this task, you must:

*   Decompose the project into functional requirements by interviewing stakeholders to develop user stories and comprehensive design criteria.
*   Design and prototype the user experience for the interactive narrative, representing the solution logic through detailed flowcharts and pseudocode.
*   Implement a modular program in an object-oriented language that integrates generative AI APIs to produce dynamic storytelling content.
*   Develop techniques to acquire, store, and validate data from API responses and user inputs to ensure system reliability and security.
*   Apply rigorous test cases to modify and debug the program, ensuring narrative consistency and technical performance.
*   Communicate the final solution using emerging digital tools to create interactive, accessible content for a diverse audience.
*   Evaluate the solution against the initial design criteria and user stories, critiquing the digital footprint, ethical implications, and potential enterprise opportunities of AI-driven systems.

text.value: investigate how hardware and software manage, control and secure access to data in networked digital systems
represent documents online as content (text), structure (markup) and presentation (styling) and explain why such representations are important
develop techniques to acquire, store and validate data from a range of sources using software, including spreadsheets and databases
analyse and visualise data interactively using a range of software, including spreadsheets and databases, to draw conclusions and make predictions by identifying trends and outliers
model and query entities and their relationships using structured data
define and decompose real-world problems with design criteria and by interviewing stakeholders to create user stories
design algorithms involving logical operators and represent them as flowcharts and pseudocode
validate algorithms and programs by comparing their output against a range of test cases
design and prototype the user experience of a digital system
generate, modify, communicate and critically evaluate alternative designs
implement, modify and debug modular programs, applying selected algorithms and data structures, including in an object-oriented programming language
evaluate existing and student solutions against the design criteria, user stories, possible future impact and opportunities for enterprise
select and use emerging digital tools and advanced features to create and communicate interactive content for a diverse audience
use simple project management tools to plan and manage individual and collaborative agile projects, accounting for risks and responsibilities
develop cyber security threat models, and explore a software, user or software supply chain vulnerability
apply the Australian Privacy Principles to critique and manage the digital footprint that existing systems and student solutions collect
